Synthetic merchant pricing model

Merchant pricing, with the cost bridge left visible.

I compared three hypothetical price structures against the same merchant mix. The point is to see who pays, what remains after modelled payment costs, and how quickly that answer changes.

Scope Every merchant and rate is authored for this project. This is not a Moneris, Visa or Mastercard quote and it is not a profitability forecast.

How I treated the numbers

A decision model, not a rate card

01

Separate price and cost

Fee revenue includes a visible commercial layer. Payment costs remain separate, so contribution margin reconciles for every merchant.

02

Weight from totals

The effective rate divides total filtered fees by total filtered sales. It does not give a small merchant the same weight as an enterprise merchant.

03

Hold pricing fixed in stress

The cost slider changes credit cost without repricing the merchant. This shows the risk between a cost change and a contract response.

04

Keep the boundary clear

Support, hardware, fraud, tax and overhead are outside the model. Contribution margin here is not operating profit.

Structure checked against public explanations from Mastercard Canada, Visa Canada and the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada. Numeric assumptions are original and synthetic.
